references.text: Describes the Salt Sea (Dead Sea) as the eastern boundary of the tribe of Judah, the same geographical reference point as in Numbers 34:12
Mentions the Salt Sea as a boundary marker and shows how the borders of the land were established in accordance with God's promise
Ezekiel's vision of the land's boundaries includes the Jordan and the eastern sea, which corresponds to the border description in Numbers
The first mention of the Salt Sea (the Valley of Siddim) in the Bible, the same geographical area referred to as a boundary
Describes the Jordan down to the Salt Sea as a boundary, parallel to the border description in Numbers 34:12
Refers to the Jordan flowing down to the Salt Sea, the same geographical context for Israel's borders
